title: Part Two, Chapter 8: The Descent into the Underworld

verses.t: And then they went off to the underworld, each carrying his blowgun, and then they went down into the underworld; they went down the steps quickly and crossed a river in a ravine. They passed through the midst of the birds, and these birds were called Molay; and they also crossed a river of pus and another of blood, and these rivers were meant for their defeat, as those of the underworld intended; but they did not tread in them, but crossed over on their blowguns. And going on from there, they came to a crossroads of four roads; and they surely knew the road to the underworld: one was black, another white, another red and another green. And from there they sent ahead a little creature called Xan; this one went to gather news. And sending it, they said to it, "Bite them one by one; first bite the first one who is seated, and finish by biting them all; and yours shall be the sucking of men's blood, and your food shall be on the roads." This was said to the Xan. "Very well," said the Xan, and then it took the black road and went straight to the first one who was seated, who was a man made of rags and dressed up, and bit him first; and he did not speak. And then it bit the second, and he did not speak either. It bit the third, who was Hun-came, and he said, complaining, when he was stung, "What is this?" "Hun-came," said the fourth who was seated, "what bit you?" "I don't know what has bitten me." It bit the next, and he said, "Ow! What is this?" "Vucub-came, what has bitten you?" said the fifth. "Ow! Ow!" said Xiquiripat. And Vucub-came said to him, "What has bitten you?" And it bit the sixth, and he said, "Ow! What is this?" "Cuchumaquic, what has bitten you?" said Xiquiripat to him. "What is this? What has bitten you?" said Cuchumaquic, when it bit the seventh, who said "Ow!" "What has bitten you, Ahalpuh?" And when it bit the eighth, who said "Ow!", Ahalpuh said to him, "What is this, Ahalcana? What bit you?" And when it bit the ninth who was seated, who said "Ow!", Ahalcana said to him, "What bit you, Chamiabac?" And when it bit the tenth, who said "Ow!", Chamiabac said to him, "What bit you, Chamiaholom?" And biting the eleventh, who said "Ow!", Chamiaholom said to him, "What bit you?" And biting the twelfth, who said "Ow!", the other said to him, "What bit you, Patán?" And biting the thirteenth, who said "Ow!", the other said to him, "What bit you, Quicxiq?" said Patán to him. And biting the fourteenth, who said "Ow!", he said to Quicrixcac, "What bit you?" And so they all said their names, and all made themselves known among themselves, saying each one's name; and one who was seated on a bench was called Holoman. And not one of their names was lost, but all of them said their names, all of them, when they were bitten by a hair from Hun-ahpu's face; for it was not really a mosquito that went to bite them all and to hear all their names for Hun-ahpu. And then, when they came to where those of the underworld were, these said to them, "Come, greet that lord." But it was not a lord, but a statue, to deceive them. And they said, "That one is only a statue." And greeting the rest, they said, "Lord Came, lord Vucub-came, lord Xiquiripat, lord Cuchumaquic, lord Ahalpuh, lord Ahalcana, lord Chamiabac, lord Chamiaholom, lord Xic, lord Patán, lord Quicre, lord Quicrixcac." This is what they said when they arrived. They saw the faces of all of them and spoke the names of all, and they did not miss or forget the name of a single one; and this was what those of the underworld wanted of them, that they should not know their names, nor find them out. "Come," they said to them, and they wanted to seat them on a seat; but they would not. "This is not our seat, for that seat is burning stone," said Hun-ahpu and Xbalanque, and they could not be beaten. "Very well," said the others. "Come, go to the house," it was said to them. And then they entered a dark house, and they were not beaten there; and this was the first punishment of the underworld. There they entered, and there those of the underworld thought to begin to triumph over them.
